root_cause.text: The driver used urb->transfer_buffer_length (the allocated buffer size) instead of urb->actual_length (the actual received data length) to validate message boundaries, allowing out-of-bounds reads when parsing CAN messages.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that actual_length is the correct size of the data passed to the driver, and the patch replaces all checks from transfer_buffer_length to actual_length, and adds a new check at the start of each message using actual_length.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a safety check to prevent out-of-bounds read when parsing CAN message headers in the EMS USB driver.
intent_record.what: Added a check before reading the message header from the receive buffer to ensure that the start offset plus the header length does not exceed the actual URB data length. If it does, the driver logs a format error and breaks out of the loop.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents accessing memory beyond the received data buffer when processing malformed or truncated CAN messages, avoiding potential out-of-bounds reads and associated crashes or security issues.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix bounds check in EMS USB CAN driver to use actual received URB length instead of buffer length to prevent out-of-bounds reads on short transfers.
intent_record.what: Changed the condition in an error check from 'if (start > urb->transfer_buffer_length)' to 'if (start > urb->actual_length)'.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the check now verifies that the byte offset does not exceed the actual number of bytes received in the URB, preventing potential out-of-bounds reads when the URB transfer is shorter than the allocated buffer.

candidates.rationale: This statement uses urb->transfer_buffer_length (the allocated buffer size) instead of urb->actual_length (the actual received data length) to validate message boundaries. An attacker could craft a CAN message with a large msg->length such that start exceeds the actual data length but still fits within the allocated buffer, leading to out-of-bounds reads.

bic_trace_step.reason: In `ems_usb_read_bulk_callback`, the check `if (start > urb->transfer_buffer_length)` uses the allocated buffer size (`transfer_buffer_length`) instead of the actual received data length (`urb->actual_length`), which is vulnerable to out-of-bounds reads when parsing messages. This is exactly the root cause described. No fix is present in this initial commit.
